title: MOAT: Securely Mitigating Rowhammer with Per-Row Activation Counters
problem: The JEDEC PRAC+ABO (Per-Row Activation Counting + Alert-Back-Off) framework for DDR5 Rowhammer mitigation is only a specification framework, not a proven secure implementation; the prior Panopticon design that inspired it is shown to be insecure via a new 'Jailbreak' attack that causes 9x more activations than the configured threshold of 128. A provably secure, low-overhead DRAM-side Rowhammer mitigation using the PRAC+ABO framework does not yet exist.
motivation: Rowhammer thresholds have dropped from 139K to 4.8K activations over the past decade and will continue falling, requiring provably secure in-DRAM mitigations that tolerate sub-100 thresholds with minimal SRAM and performance overhead.
method: MOAT (Mitigating Rowhammer with Dual Thresholds) uses per-row activation counters (PRAC) with two internal thresholds: ETH (Eligibility Threshold) for proactive mitigation during REF operations and ATH (ALERT Threshold) for triggering the ALERT-Back-Off reactive protocol. Instead of Panopticon's 8-entry per-bank queue (which loses counter information and enables Jailbreak), MOAT tracks only a single entry per bank via a Current Tracked Addr (CTA) register that always holds the row with the highest counter value, plus a Current Mitigated Addr (CMA) register, requiring only 7 bytes of SRAM per bank total. A safe counter-reset-on-refresh mechanism preserves counter integrity across refresh groups by copying boundary-row counters to 2-byte SRAM registers. The Ratchet attack analysis, exploiting the inter-ALERT activations permitted by JEDEC ABO specifications, establishes that MOAT with ATH=64 can safely tolerate a Rowhammer threshold of 99.
key_novelty: Replacing Panopticon's multi-entry queue with a single-entry CTA register that tracks the highest-activation-count row, enabling a provably secure dual-threshold (ETH/ATH) design with only 7 bytes SRAM per bank.
contributions: Jailbreak attack demonstrating Panopticon (the basis of PRAC+ABO) is insecure, inflicting 1152 activations (9x over threshold=128) for both deterministic and randomized variants.
MOAT design with dual ETH/ATH thresholds and single-entry CTA/CMA tracking achieving provably secure Rowhammer mitigation.
Ratchet attack analysis quantifying the impact of JEDEC-permitted inter-ALERT activations on tolerated TRH, establishing ATH=64 tolerates TRH=99.
Evaluation on 15 SPEC-2017 and 6 GAP benchmarks showing 0.28% average slowdown and 7 bytes SRAM per bank for ATH=64.

metrics.speedup: 0.28% average slowdown (ATH=64) over no-ALERT baseline on SPEC2017+GAP
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.3% increase in total DRAM activations; <0.5% total DRAM energy increase
metrics.other: TRH tolerated: 99 (ATH=64); Jailbreak: 1152 ACTs vs 128 threshold on Panopticon

limitations: MOAT is restricted to ABO mitigation level 1 (single RFM per ALERT), limiting its ability to handle higher mitigation levels; RowPress attacks are explicitly out of scope.
primary_theme: provably secure in-DRAM Rowhammer mitigation via dual-threshold per-row counting
